items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Each change is a small guard, `if not self.field.is_cached(rel_obj):`, written in the style of the surrounding code with the existing names kept. The intent is clear from the API name, and the nearby comments already explain the manual reverse-cache management.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It reuses the existing field cache API (`is_cached`) and adds no new bookkeeping. The same two-line guard appears in three parallel get_prefetch_queryset methods, but those already repeat this loop, so this is not new copy-paste. There is no dead code or debug output.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: There is no new error handling to judge, and no swallowed errors or magic constants. When the relation is not cached, the parent is still assigned as before, so plain prefetches behave the same. All 85 pass-to-pass tests pass.

items.name: Guard is conditional and covers the one-to-one variant
items.name_zh: 仅在已缓存时跳过回填，并考虑一对一情形
items.evidence: The guard skips the assignment only when the child already has the relation cached, so plain prefetches still fill the reverse relation. It is applied to the reverse-FK manager and also to `ReverseOneToOneDescriptor.get_prefetch_queryset` via `self.related.field.is_cached(rel_obj)`, which covers the one-to-one variant (`user.profile.user`).
